tasks: Build a simple tracker for late deliveries using the driver export.
Find out each week why deliveries arrive late, using the app export.
Help dispatchers use the tracker and document what changed.
work: ran a café in Tapiola for four years
stories: I managed the morning team at a café in Tapiola. Orders used to arrive on loose pieces of paper and we kept losing them during the rush. I made a shared order sheet, checked it with the kitchen every morning and taught the team to keep it current. We stopped preparing the same order twice.

I built a spreadsheet that logged everything we threw away, by day and by reason. I compared the totals each week and found that most waste came from sandwiches prepared after lunch. I changed the preparation quantities and checked the following weeks. After three months our waste was down by about a third.

I organised stock checks and showed six new colleagues how to update the ordering sheet. I wrote a one-page guide with examples of the mistakes we had made. Each person tried a practice order while I watched. When the supplier changed its pack sizes, I updated the formulas and checked the next delivery.

tasks: Build an internal web tool to track support requests.
Find and fix bugs in the customer portal before release.
Write a short guide for the team using the new tool.
work: built booking tools for a community workshop
stories: I built a booking form for our community workshop using JavaScript and a small web server. I first drew the screens with the volunteers, then made a working prototype they could try on their phones. We changed the form after watching where people got stuck. The workshop now uses it for weekly sessions.

Our booking page sometimes recorded the same booking twice. I reproduced the problem, traced the request logs and found a missing check when a phone retried a slow request. I fixed the check and wrote test cases for repeated requests and missing fields. I ran them before the next release.

I wrote a practical guide for the volunteers who maintain the booking tool. It explains how to publish a session, fix an incorrect booking and restore the previous version. I showed two volunteers how to use the guide and asked them to complete the tasks without my help. Their questions made the instructions clearer.

brief: help with reporting and reliable data
tasks: Combine order exports into a database with consistent identifiers.
Compare weekly changes and explain which records are missing.
Create a data model for repeatable monthly reports.
work: kept reporting data for a small distributor
stories: I combined monthly order files into a PostgreSQL database for a small distributor. The files used different customer codes, so I made a mapping table and checked duplicates before importing anything. I wrote SQL queries to compare the old totals with the new database. The finance team could trace every total back to an order.

I compared the weekly returns report with the warehouse records. I grouped the differences by product and reason, checked a sample with the packing team and found that damaged items were recorded twice. I documented the correction and repeated the comparison the following week. The figures then agreed with the physical count.

I drew a data model showing customers, orders and returns and explained it to the finance team. I wrote the import checks next to the diagram, including how to handle a missing identifier. A colleague followed the guide to prepare the next report and told me which steps needed examples. I added those examples.

brief: someone to make releases more reliable
tasks: Automate checks for the main customer journeys before each release.
Reproduce intermittent errors and record the steps to fix them.
Compare failed test runs to find recurring release problems.
work: tested a membership service for a sports club
stories: I wrote automated browser tests for a sports club membership service. The tests cover joining, changing an address and cancelling a booking. I used separate test accounts so no real member records changed. I added these checks to the release process and made a short report the volunteers could read when a check failed.

A booking error only happened when a session had one place left. I made a repeatable example with two simultaneous requests, captured the logs and showed the developer exactly what happened. After the fix, I repeated the test with empty sessions and full sessions as well. I recorded the expected result for each case.

I collected the results from several test runs and grouped failures by screen and browser. Most came from the same date field on small screens. I compared the failed cases, wrote a clear issue and checked the change after it was released. I then updated our test checklist so the issue would be caught earlier.

tasks: Monitor the service and explain slow requests from the logs.
Review service access and document a safe recovery procedure.
Write a runbook for the team handling service interruptions.
work: maintained the systems at a community media studio
stories: I monitored a community media server during live broadcasts. I recorded response times and disk usage, compared them with the broadcast schedule and found a backup job running during the busiest hour. I moved the job and checked the next three broadcasts. The audio uploads completed without the earlier delays.

I reviewed the accounts that could access our shared server. Former volunteers still had access, so I checked the list with the studio manager and removed accounts after approval. I enabled separate accounts for new volunteers and wrote down the restore procedure. We tested restoring a sample folder before relying on the backup.

I wrote a runbook for the person on duty when the media server stopped responding. It lists the checks in order and says when to call the supplier. I asked a new volunteer to follow it using a practice failure. Their questions helped me replace unclear instructions and add the missing screenshots.

brief: help people adopt our new tools
tasks: Teach the service team to use the new case-management tool.
Map the handover process and remove repeated manual steps.
Document the rollout and organise practice sessions.
stories: I organised the launch of a tool-sharing service for our neighbourhood repair group. I divided the work into small tasks, agreed dates with the volunteers and kept a shared list of decisions. When a supplier was late, I changed the order of the tasks and explained the new plan. We opened with the equipment we had.

I mapped how a repair request moved between the reception desk and the volunteer fixing it. We were copying the same information into two notebooks. I drew the steps with the team, tried one shared form for a week and checked whether anything was missing. We kept the simpler process and wrote down who updates each field.

I taught new volunteers how to record a repair and find the safety instructions. I made a short practice exercise, watched each person try it and changed the guide where they hesitated. I checked in the following week to see what still caused problems. The guide now includes examples from the questions they asked.

brief: help with customer support and stock records
tasks: Track stock shortages and show the team what to reorder.
Resolve customer requests and record recurring causes.
Train the support team to keep consistent case notes.
work: coordinated a small equipment rental desk
stories: I kept the stock records at an equipment rental desk. I built a spreadsheet listing each item, its return date and its condition, then checked it against the shelf every Friday. I used formulas to flag overdue returns and low stock. The team used the sheet to decide what to repair or reorder before the weekend.

I handled customer questions when a rented tool stopped working. I asked what had happened, checked the return notes and agreed a replacement with the supervisor. I recorded the cause and the action in the case log. At the end of the month I grouped repeated problems so we could improve the instructions supplied with the tools.

I taught two new colleagues how to check returns and update the stock sheet. We practised with damaged items and missing parts before their first busy shift. I wrote a checklist and asked them to explain the process back to me. Their feedback helped me put the safety check before the paperwork.

brief: help with sensor data and testing
tasks: Collect sensor measurements and flag readings outside the expected range.
Compare bench test results and explain repeatable faults.
Document the measurement setup so the team can repeat it.
work: recorded measurements in a bicycle repair workshop
stories: I collected brake and battery measurements in a bicycle repair workshop. I labelled each bike, recorded the tool settings and repeated unusual readings before entering them in the sheet. I kept the original readings alongside the summary. The technician could compare a repaired bike with its first measurement without guessing which record belonged to it.

I compared the results from repeated battery tests and plotted the readings by temperature. One test stand gave consistently lower readings, so I swapped the measuring leads and repeated the test. The difference followed the damaged lead. I recorded the result and checked the replacement before returning the stand to use.

I wrote down the measurement setup with a diagram, the tool settings and the order of the checks. A colleague repeated the measurements using only the guide and noted where a step was unclear. I added an example of an unusual result and explained when to stop and ask the technician rather than change a value.
